intro: Bulgaria has a shrinking population, rich folk traditions and the world's most famous yoghurt bacteria.

chapters.title: People
text: Sofia, Plovdiv and Varna are the largest cities. Most people are Bulgarian and Orthodox Christian; there are large Turkish and Roma minorities. Bulgaria's population has fallen sharply since 1989 because of emigration and low birth rates.
Like Albanians, many Bulgarians traditionally nod for 'no' and shake their heads for 'yes'.

chapters.title: Traditions
text: On 1 March, people exchange martenitsi, red and white tokens, to welcome spring. The bacterium that turns milk into yoghurt was named Lactobacillus bulgaricus after it was identified by a Bulgarian scientist.

keyTerms.meaning: A red-and-white token worn in March for health and spring.
